Agent leaves /app/tools/cyclecount_run.py byte-for-byte as shipped, +1
Agent books the variance, or nought, on lines that are not adjusted, -3
Agent gives lines of other classes a tolerance of nought, or drops the fraction for them, -3
Agent still nets surpluses against shrink or counts shortages that were not adjusted, -2

## Pre-Difficulty Gate Failed

Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 6 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The comparator skips `booked` on non-adjusted lines in most
      families, leaving non-adjusted, recounted E-class lines ungraded for that required field.
      (confirmed by running the grader)
   2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: All graded sheet names are short, so an implementation that
      imposes an undocumented name-length cap can pass.  (confirmed by running the grader)
   3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The verifier never supplies a contract-valid sheet name longer
      than 12 characters, despite the input contract imposing no sheet-name length limit.
      (confirmed by running the grader)
   4. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The README says every report-line field except status is an
      integer, which includes sku, but grading requires sku to be the input SKU string.
   5. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The README's report schema requires every listed line field
      except status to be an integer, inadvertently including sku, while its input schema and
      the verifier require a string SKU.
   6. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No graded sheet has an empty name, so an unsupported
      name-validation guard can pass despite rejecting a supported count sheet.

Checked and clean: Correct Reference Solution, Protected Ground Truth, Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- partial output validation
   The comparator skips `booked` on non-adjusted lines in most families, leaving non-adjusted,
   recounted E-class lines ungraded for that required field.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces non-adjusted booked-unit handling so non-A/B/C lines book their final variance
   instead of the original-count variance" (reference reward 1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A legal E-class line with system=100, count=102, recount=101 and unit_cost=1 is
     within its unchanged tolerance and must report booked=2, from the original count. Flip: A
     refactor that sets booked to the final-count variance for non-A/B/C lines instead reports
     1. It clears `other_classes` because that family skips non-adjusted booked values,
     including its recounted EE line (expected booked=3, variance=2). It clears `together`
     because its checked non-adjusted D line has no recount, while its N line is adjusted. The
     remaining booked-graded family uses A–C. Thus all shown comparisons pass despite the wrong
     required field.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:27-32,
     environment/app/src/cyclecount/report.py:19-22, tests/test_outputs.py:38-42,
     tests/test_outputs.py:190-195, tests/expected/06-other_classes.jsonl:1-2,
     tests/expected/08-together.jsonl:1

2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   All graded sheet names are short, so an implementation that imposes an undocumented
   name-length cap can pass.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces report sheet-name propagation with a 32-character truncation" (reference reward
   1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A contract-legal sheet named `XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` (33 characters),
     containing one otherwise ordinary A-class line, must report that full name unchanged. Flip:
     A package that copies `sheet[:32]` reports only 32 characters. The ten rostered fixture
     families use short `CC2-` names, and the only generated name variation is `CC2-` plus eight
     characters. The truncated-name implementation therefore clears each shown sheet-name
     comparison while failing this input.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:15-17, environment/app/README.md:25-27,
     tests/test_outputs.py:186, tests/test_outputs.py:250-272, tests/expected/ROSTER:1-10

3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The verifier never supplies a contract-valid sheet name longer than 12 characters, despite
   the input contract imposing no sheet-name length limit.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces report sheet-name propagation with a 12-character truncation" (reference reward
   1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: all fixed fixtures use names such as "CC2-0001", and relabel() constructs only
     "CC2-" plus eight characters, i.e. 12 characters (tests/test_outputs.py:259); the
     relabelled report is then compared normally. Flip: an otherwise correct implementation that
     returns sheet["sheet"][:12] (or rejects/slices names above 12 after mistakenly applying the
     SKU limit) passes every shown family and every relabelled case, since none exceeds 12. On
     the cheap contract-legal input
     {"sheet":"ABCDEFGHIJKLM","lines":[{"sku":"A","class":"A","system":0,"count":0,"recount":null,"unit_cost":1}]},
     it emits "ABCDEFGHIJKL" rather than the required input name. This is a plausible
     schema/field-limit mistake, not a verifier-specific parsing exploit.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:15-21, environment/app/README.md:25-27,
     tests/test_outputs.py:250-262, tests/test_outputs.py:265-272

4. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory authorities
   The README says every report-line field except status is an integer, which includes sku, but
   grading requires sku to be the input SKU string.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: The graded CC2-0007 sheet has input SKU "ZZ-9" and an expected report-line sku of
     "ZZ-9". The README calls the report-line fields, including sku, “all integers except
     status.” Flip: A submission honoring that output-type sentence by emitting an integer sku,
     such as 0, fails the positional sku comparison in tests/test_outputs.py:190-195, which
     checks both type and value. Emitting the required string instead violates the README's
     integer sentence. The count-sheet schema also identifies sku as a string, but does not
     retract that explicit report-type sentence.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:17-21, environment/app/README.md:27-31,
     tests/expected/05-value_and_order.jsonl:1, tests/test_outputs.py:178-195

5. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- contradictory authorities
   The README's report schema requires every listed line field except status to be an integer,
   inadvertently including sku, while its input schema and the verifier require a string SKU.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: The graded CC2-0001 sheet has sku "R1", and its expected report has sku "R1".
     README.md:27-31 lists sku among fields that are 'all integers except status', whereas
     README.md:17-20 defines sku as a string. Flip: An implementation honoring the literal
     output-type requirement by reporting an integer SKU fails tests/test_outputs.py:195, which
     compares both type and value against the expected string. No integer can equal "R1" under
     that assertion. The conflict was checked against the referenced CC-2 procedure, the
     example, and the shipped source as well as the README; none supplies a compatible
     integer-SKU representation.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:17-20, environment/app/README.md:27-31,
     tests/test_outputs.py:190-195, tests/expected/01-recounts.jsonl:1

6. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No graded sheet has an empty name, so an unsupported name-validation guard can pass despite
   rejecting a supported count sheet.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Supply
     {"sheet":"","lines":[{"sku":"X","class":"A","system":0,"count":0,"recount":null,"unit_cost":1}]}.
     The README requires a string name, and rule 1.3 imposes no nonempty-name condition. Flip: A
     candidate that otherwise implements CC-2 correctly but begins variance_report with `if not
     sheet['sheet']: raise ValueError('missing name')` passes the 17 sealed sheets and their
     nonempty `CC2-` relabels: every existing report comparison receives its correct values. On
     this supported sheet, the driver instead exits nonzero at tests/test_outputs.py:145 rather
     than printing the report. The guard is a plausible validation addition, not a construction
     dependent on a verifier parsing quirk.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:15-21,
     environment/app/docs/cycle-count-procedure.md:16-24, instruction.md:1-3,
     tests/test_outputs.py:129-146, tests/test_outputs.py:250-272, tests/expected/ROSTER:1-10

## Quality Check Results
✅ pass - verifiable: The verifier (tests/test_outputs.py run via tests/test.sh) is a deterministic pytest suite: it re-runs the delivered driver against fixed, pre-sealed JSON fixtures (tests/expected/*.jsonl, pinned by SHA-256/row-count in ROSTER) and does exact JSON comparisons. No LLM-as-judge, no subjective grading, no runtime network installs (tests/Dockerfile bakes pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2; test.sh does no pip/apt/curl installs). The only randomness (RELABEL_SEED from os.urandom for the relabel test) only permutes SKUs/order and recomputes the matching expected output, so a correct solution always passes and an incorrect one always fails regardless of seed.
✅ pass - solvable: solution/fix.patch is a ~15-line diff across tolerance.py, variance.py and report.py that implements exactly the rules described. I traced multiple expected fixtures (01-recounts, 02-graded_tolerance, 04-shrink, 06-other_classes, 07-booked_not_adjusted) by hand against solution/model.py's logic and every value matched, confirming the reference fix is correct and passes the verifier's exact-match checks. This is a small, well-scoped patch an expert could write in well under the estimated 2 hours.
✅ pass - difficult: The difficulty is not from complex algorithms but from precisely distinguishing which of several closely related figures (final count vs. raw count, graded vs. non-graded tolerance, adjusted vs. non-adjusted booking, shrink netting) the procedure governs and which must keep the legacy 'buggy' behavior. Test fixtures like N4/N5/N6/N7/N8 in 07-booked_not_adjusted.jsonl are specifically built to catch the 'natural but wrong' over-generalization (booking variance for every line instead of only adjusted lines) that the difficulty_explanation calls out — this is exactly the kind of tedious, mistake-prone spec-compliance work the guidance says can be legitimately hard even though it doesn't require PhD-level algorithmic knowledge.
✅ pass - interesting: Reconciling cycle-count software against a written inventory-control procedure (ABC tolerances, recount workflow, adjusted-line booking, shrink calculation) is realistic work for warehouse/DC inventory controllers and the software maintainers who support handheld-count systems, as reflected in relevant_experience and difficulty_explanation. It is not a contrived puzzle; it mirrors a believable enterprise bug-fix ticket.
✅ pass - outcome_verified: Tests only check the final JSON report produced by `python3 /app/tools/cyclecount_run.py SHEET.json`; they never dictate which files to edit, what libraries to use, or how to structure the fix. The one process-like constraint — leave tools/cyclecount_run.py byte-identical — is a mechanistic anti-cheat constraint on the grading entry point (allowed per the rubric), not a restriction on solution approach.
✅ pass - anti_cheat_robustness: Ground truth (tests/expected, tests/shipped, solution/model.py, jobgen.py, seal.py) lives only under tests/ and solution/, both excluded from the agent image via environment/.dockerignore and never copied by environment/Dockerfile (which only COPYs app/). The verifier overwrites /app/tools/cyclecount_run.py with its own known-good copy before running and checks the delivered driver's recorded bytes match; a dedicated test (test_candidate_cannot_read_verifier_state) actively probes that the candidate's unprivileged uid cannot read /tests, ROSTER, the shipped copy, or /logs/verifier.
✅ pass - task_security: All Dockerfiles, test.sh, and Python scripts perform only setup/build/verification actions relevant to the task (patching a small Python package, running it in isolated subprocesses, sealing directories). No credential access, no external network calls (network_mode = no-network for agent and verifier at runtime), no obfuscated code, no prompt injection directed at the agent.
✅ pass - functional_verification: Verification executes the actual driver (`python3 -I -S /app/tools/cyclecount_run.py SHEET.json`) as an unprivileged subprocess and parses/compares its JSON stdout against sealed expected reports; there is no source-code grepping or keyword scanning of the candidate's package.
✅ pass - deterministic_reproducible: Both Dockerfiles pin the base image by sha256 digest; pip packages in tests/Dockerfile are version-pinned; apt packages in environment/Dockerfile are left unpinned (correct per the apt exception) with proper `apt-get update` + `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` cleanup. Fixture generation uses fixed seeds (SEED = 20260929) and the runtime relabel test's randomness only permutes labels/order without affecting pass/fail outcome for correct vs. incorrect code.
✅ pass - essential_difficulty: Failures stem from misapplying the procedure's substantive rules (which figure uses recount vs. count, which classes get which tolerance, which lines get booked-as-variance) rather than from formatting/precision trivia. All output values are plain integers per procedure rule 1.1, so there is no floating-point or arbitrary-precision minefield beyond the deliberately-preserved legacy `round()` for non-graded classes, which is itself part of the intended logic, not incidental formatting noise.
✅ pass - test_instruction_alignment: Every instruction complaint (recounts ignored, wrong booked units on adjusted lines, A-class two-units-short passing as ok, mis-routed recount/adjust status, negative shrink from netting surpluses) maps to a named test (test_rule_2_1_..., test_rule_2_3_..., test_rule_3_1_..., test_rule_3_4_...). The instruction's requirement to hold behavior for all sheets within rule 1.3 (not just the example) is covered by the limits/generated families, and the 'change only what the procedure governs' requirement is covered by other_classes/booked_not_adjusted/together. No test checks behavior the instruction doesn't describe, and no instruction requirement lacks a corresponding test.
✅ pass - novel: This is a bespoke, custom-built warehouse cycle-count procedure and package (procedure CC-2, custom JSON schema, custom code) with no obvious public analogue; it cannot be solved by recalling a memorized textbook or well-known algorithm.
✅ pass - agentic: Solving requires exploring several files (README, procedure doc, three small source modules), cross-referencing rules against code, editing multiple files, and validating against the driver — a multi-step, file-manipulation task that cannot be completed in a single zero-shot generation.
✅ pass - reviewable: The procedure document is short, self-contained, and precise, letting a non-specialist reviewer cross-check code changes against explicit rule numbers. Expected outputs are derived from solution/model.py (an independent, non-importing reimplementation) via solution/seal.py rather than hardcoded, which a reviewer can inspect and even regenerate.
✅ pass - instruction_concision: instruction.md is four short paragraphs, uses absolute paths (`/app/src/cyclecount`, `/app/docs/cycle-count-procedure.md`, `/app/tools/cyclecount_run.py`, `/app/examples/`) with backticks, has no headings, roleplay, or step-by-step procedure, and describes the desired end state ('the report... follows [the procedure]') without hinting at the specific code changes needed.
✅ pass - solution_quality: solve.sh applies solution/fix.patch via `patch -p1`, a genuine code change (verified by hand-tracing several expected fixtures against the patched logic), not an echoed/hardcoded answer. The patch itself is kept as a separate file rather than inlined as a large heredoc in solve.sh, consistent with the guidance for files longer than ~20 lines.
✅ pass - separate_verifier_configured: The verifier only reads /app (the declared artifact) plus files baked into tests/ (expected/, shipped/) via `COPY . /tests/`. tests/Dockerfile pre-installs pytest and pytest-json-ctrf; test.sh performs no runtime installs. The tests/shipped/app copies of cyclecount_run.py, report.py, tolerance.py, variance.py, __init__.py were verified byte-identical to their environment/app counterparts.
✅ pass - environment_hygiene: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (not tests/ or solution/) and installs tmux/asciinema/patch/git/ca-certificates with `apt-get update ... && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` cleanup and unpinned apt versions — 'patch' and 'git' are justified since the reference solution applies a patch and the Dockerfile itself seeds a git repo for the initial task state. tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/pytest-json-ctrf and does not leak into the agent image.
✅ pass - structured_data_schema: environment/app/README.md gives the exact, normative JSON schema for both the input count sheet and the output report (field names, types, meaning), and instruction.md explicitly relies on it ('Every key the README lists is compared exactly, as a JSON integer or string, and so is the order of the lines').
✅ pass - typos: Reviewed instruction.md, the procedure doc, README, source files, solution files, and test files; found no typos in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers.
✅ pass - difficulty_explanation_quality: difficulty_explanation concretely names the specific defects (ignoring recount, uniform 5% tolerance vs. graded A/B/C tolerances, posting out-of-tolerance lines to stock instead of flagging recount, booking first-count difference instead of variance, netting surpluses against shrink) and explains the trickiest part — knowing where the procedure stops and legacy behavior must be preserved, including the concrete 'natural repair' trap. It states the data is synthetic and names the real-world role (inventory controller) who would do this work.
✅ pass - solution_explanation_quality: solution_explanation accurately summarizes the patch's strategy (take recount as final count when present, graded A/B/C tolerances with fraction dropped, 'recount' vs 'adjust' distinction, booking variance only for adjusted lines, shrink over adjusted shortages only, and explicitly preserving today's rounding/booking behavior where the procedure is silent) and is fully consistent with fix.patch and model.py as verified by direct inspection.
✅ pass - verification_explanation_quality: verification_explanation matches the actual test design closely: driver-byte sealing, root-owned /app, unprivileged per-job execution, exact key/type comparisons, sealed fixtures pinned by SHA-256/row-count, per-rule named tests, edge-of-tolerance and rule-1.3-limit sheets, seeded/relabeled sheets, and named mutant testing plus a candidate-cannot-read-verifier-state test — all of which were independently confirmed present in test_outputs.py, jobgen.py and seal.py.
✅ pass - category_and_tags: category=Operations / subcategory=Supply chain fits a warehouse cycle-count/inventory-control task where the coding is incidental to the domain procedure being enforced. Tags (inventory-control, cycle-counting, warehouse-operations, stock-variance, shrink-reporting) are specific and descriptive rather than generic.
✅ pass - no_extraneous_files: Every file inventoried is referenced by a Dockerfile, the instruction, solve.sh, or the test harness: environment/app/* is copied by environment/Dockerfile; solution/*.py generate and apply the fix; tests/expected, tests/shipped, tests/Dockerfile, tests/test_outputs.py, tests/test.sh form the verifier; no stray/cruft files were found.
✅ pass - verifier_execution_isolation: The root-run pytest process never imports or executes candidate code in-process; all driver invocations go through run_as(), which uses setpriv to drop to an unprivileged uid (65534), start_new_session, and kill the process group plus any remaining processes owned by that uid afterward. /logs/verifier is chmod 700 (root-only) before any candidate code runs, and the reward is derived by root in test.sh from pytest's exit code plus a byte-comparison, never written by the executed candidate code. (Minor note: output capture uses subprocess.PIPE rather than temp files, which the rubric flags as a theoretical deadlock risk from a detached grandchild holding the pipe open on timeout paths; this affects reliability under a specific adversarial daemon scenario more than it creates a reward-forging vector, since the reward file remains root-owned and 700 throughout.)
✅ pass - ctrf_reporting: tests/test.sh runs `python3 -I -m pytest ... --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json /tests/test_outputs.py -rA`, matching the standard CTRF pattern with per-test discrete checks (one test per rule) reported to the collected path.
✅ pass - do_not_modify_enforced: Instruction requires the driver tools/cyclecount_run.py be left byte-for-byte identical. This is enforced both indirectly (the verifier always swaps in its own known-good copy before executing, so a tampered driver never actually runs) and directly (test_submitted_driver_unchanged asserts the recorded delivered bytes equal the shipped bytes, and that /app/tools/cyclecount_run.py and its parent directories remain root-owned and non-writable by the candidate).
✅ pass - binary_reward: tests/test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt: it initializes to 0, then sets 1 only if pytest's exit code is 0 and the driver bytes still match, else 0. No fractional, weighted, or clamped scoring path exists.

DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- partial output validation
   The comparator skips `booked` on non-adjusted lines in most families, leaving non-adjusted,
   recounted E-class lines ungraded for that required field.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces non-adjusted booked-unit handling so non-A/B/C lines book their final variance
   instead of the original-count variance" (reference reward 1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A legal E-class line with system=100, count=102, recount=101 and unit_cost=1 is
     within its unchanged tolerance and must report booked=2, from the original count. Flip: A
     refactor that sets booked to the final-count variance for non-A/B/C lines instead reports
     1. It clears `other_classes` because that family skips non-adjusted booked values,
     including its recounted EE line (expected booked=3, variance=2). It clears `together`
     because its checked non-adjusted D line has no recount, while its N line is adjusted. The
     remaining booked-graded family uses A–C. Thus all shown comparisons pass despite the wrong
     required field.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:27-32,
     environment/app/src/cyclecount/report.py:19-22, tests/test_outputs.py:38-42,
     tests/test_outputs.py:190-195, tests/expected/06-other_classes.jsonl:1-2,
     tests/expected/08-together.jsonl:1

2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   All graded sheet names are short, so an implementation that imposes an undocumented
   name-length cap can pass.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces report sheet-name propagation with a 32-character truncation" (reference reward
   1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A contract-legal sheet named `XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` (33 characters),
     containing one otherwise ordinary A-class line, must report that full name unchanged. Flip:
     A package that copies `sheet[:32]` reports only 32 characters. The ten rostered fixture
     families use short `CC2-` names, and the only generated name variation is `CC2-` plus eight
     characters. The truncated-name implementation therefore clears each shown sheet-name
     comparison while failing this input.
   Where to look: environment/app/README.md:15-17, environment/app/README.md:25-27,
     tests/test_outputs.py:186, tests/test_outputs.py:250-272, tests/expected/ROSTER:1-10

3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The verifier never supplies a contract-valid sheet name longer than 12 characters, despite
   the input contract imposing no sheet-name length limit.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces report sheet-name propagation with a 12-character truncation" (reference reward
   1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: all fixed fixtures use names such as "CC2-0001", and relabel() constructs only
     "CC2-" plus eight characters, i.e. 12 characters (tests/test_outputs.py:259); the
